rule: existential instantiation of the thought and its bearer, then of the non-living actual thing; universal instantiation of the comparison and convertibility
meaning: If some thought occurs, every occurring thought has a bearer, every bearer of an occurring thought lives, some actual thing does not live, whatever lives is more noble than any non-living actual thing, and a grade of nobility is also a grade of goodness and truth, then some thing is more good, some more true and some more noble than another (the quarta via's grades premise). Every premise is open; the thinker witnesses only the comparison, not any maximum. Omitting any premise has a finite countermodel; one joint model with a thinker and a stone satisfies all premises.
